### HTML scraping

Does including header content improve predictions? Answer the question and provide quantitative evidence supporting your answer.

The goal of this analysis was to check whether including HTML headers in training data (2,165 webpages) improved binary class prediction accuracy. Webpages were either classified as having "No relevant content" or "Relevant claim content." We discovered that including header content does not improve prediction accuracy. After including headers, the Ridge regularized logistic regression model accuracy decreased from 0.797 (baseline) to 0.771. Although these numbers are very similar, we can conclude that headers do not help prediction accuracy, so are not needed in the training data.  

### Bigrams

Do bigrams capture additional information relevant to the classification of interest? Answer the question, **briefly** describe what analysis you conducted to arrive at your answer, and provide quantitative evidence supporting your answer.

Bigrams do not appear to capture additional information helpful to the classification of whether or not a claim is or isn't relevant. We first extracted the important text from each of the claims, and turned each individual word into a single "token" or unigram. Based on these single words in each claim, we predicted whether or not the claim contained relevant content or not. We then repeated this process again this time using the two word phrases (bigrams) in each claim as well along with information about how strongly the individual words support one predicted class over another. As mentioned above, the baseline logistic regression model had a classification accuracy of 0.797. Interestingly enough, with the bigrams, the accuracy also dropped to 0.771, which could be due to the distortion of the stacked model. We reduced data complexity twice before stacking the models which may have created components with little discriminative power.
